title: Continuous close-world scale coordinate driven directly by wheel input

scope.subject: Reuse camera-controls lerpLookAt with the existing ProceduralPlanets close-world renderer so wheel delta continuously drives the Approach to Surface camera path while UniversePhase remains only a semantic/rendering boundary

research_summary: The current Continuous Scale implementation centralizes wheel ownership correctly, but still converts accumulated wheel input into discrete Approach/Orbit/Atmosphere/Surface phase transitions and then asks camera-controls to animate to fixed shots. camera-controls v3.1.2 already exposes lerpLookAt specifically for interpolation between two complete look-at states, while the existing R3F host and ProceduralPlanets world remain mounted across close-world phases. The smallest globally-correct change is therefore to add one normalized close-world scale coordinate, derive semantic phases from that coordinate only at boundaries, and let the existing camera-controls instance continuously interpolate the same shot anchors as wheel input arrives. No second camera loop, tween library, renderer, or world model is required.

sources.finding: The exact installed camera-controls line provides setLookAt and lerpLookAt; lerpLookAt interpolates between two complete position/target states with an explicit t in [0,1], so the existing camera authority can be driven by a continuous product scale coordinate without another animation system.

The already-adopted ProceduralPlanets renderer remains the close-world visual authority and can stay mounted across Approach, Orbit, Atmosphere and Surface; continuous camera progress does not require another planet or terrain renderer.
Pinned MIT YEIS remains the large-scale galaxy/system spatial authority. The new coordinate must stop at the existing System/Approach handoff rather than duplicating YEIS physical navigation.
OpenSpace demonstrates continuous focus-relative scale travel as a product interaction model. Only the interaction principle is reused; no OpenSpace code or renderer is introduced.

search_ladder.conclusion: Retain pinned MIT YEIS for galaxy/system scale and its focus model. Do not replace the selected universe engine merely to obtain smoother close-world camera motion.
Keep the single existing R3F Canvas and scene lifecycle; the continuous coordinate is product state passed into the current camera component.
Keep ProceduralPlanets mounted as the existing close-world renderer across the coordinate range; only semantic Surface activation and terrain anchoring remain boundary behavior.
Use camera-controls lerpLookAt on the existing control instance to interpolate adjacent shot anchors directly from normalized scale progress instead of writing a custom RAF/tween camera.

coverage_matrix.capability: Wheel delta produces visible sub-phase camera motion before crossing a semantic boundary
coverage_matrix.decision: Drive a normalized close-world coordinate directly from wheel delta and pass it to the existing camera-controls instance.

coverage_matrix.capability: Approach, Orbit and Atmosphere remain one continuous visual world
coverage_matrix.decision: Keep the same PlanetScene/ProceduralPlanets instance mounted; semantic phase changes do not replace the close-world renderer.

coverage_matrix.capability: Surface retains terrain-aware landing and renderer fallback semantics
coverage_matrix.decision: Interpolate toward the existing Surface shot/frame near the final coordinate while retaining live/fallback Surface activation as the semantic boundary.

coverage_matrix.capability: Reverse wheel movement is exactly reversible without queued phase animations
coverage_matrix.decision: Scale position moves monotonically with signed wheel delta; adjacent camera anchors are evaluated from the same coordinate in either direction.

coverage_matrix.capability: One camera and one wheel authority remain
coverage_matrix.decision: Keep camera-controls wheel ACTION disabled and continue routing wheel only through UniverseApp.

decision.rationale: Introduce only a normalized close-world scale coordinate and adjacent-shot interpolation. Keep YEIS as large-scale spatial authority, camera-controls as the only close-world camera executor, R3F as the only host, ProceduralPlanets as the close-world renderer, and UniversePhase as semantic/rendering state rather than the source of camera jumps.
decision.fallback: If the final Surface terrain frame is not ready, interpolate only through the stable Atmosphere/pre-landing anchor and hold the final fraction until the existing Surface frame/fallback contract is available; never spawn another camera or terrain authority.
